items.title: Starts reliably, every time
items.body: Meridian repairs its own start-at-login registration on every launch, and comes back when your machine wakes instead of at a fixed hour.

items.title: GitHub tasks from your plan
items.body: New issues are filed, assigned to you and placed on your board - reconnect GitHub in Settings once to grant the permission this needs.

items.title: Steadier around restarts
items.body: Your database and your signed-in session both come through a restart intact.

items.title: Ollama Cloud, free to use
items.body: A no-subscription way to draft with AI, and the one we now recommend if you don't already have a subscription.

items.title: Usage reporting you can switch off
items.body: Settings shows exactly what daily usage reporting sends, with its own switch separate from error reports.

items.title: Sign-in and drafting fixes
items.body: Signing in sticks on a cold start, and a brief provider hiccup no longer stops your day being written.

items.title: The tour stays out of your way
items.body: It no longer covers the very buttons it asks you to press.

items.title: Work logs update as you post
items.body: A row you just filed no longer keeps saying it is a draft waiting for you.

items.title: Fewer false permission warnings
items.body: A permission has to read as off for five minutes before Meridian mentions it.

items.title: Notifications work on Windows
items.body: Buttons and the reply box now do what they already did on Mac.

items.title: Replay the guided tour
items.body: Settings - Account - Show me around brings it back any time.

items.title: The Windows dashboard behaves
items.body: It opens with its title bar and window controls intact instead of covering the whole screen.

items.title: Setup picks up where you left off
items.body: Closing the wizard part-way no longer means starting again from the first card.

items.title: Signing in sticks
items.body: Your session is no longer quietly dropped every time Meridian restarts.

items.title: Told when your summary is ready
items.body: Meridian tells you, instead of leaving you to go and look.

items.title: A guided walkthrough
items.body: Meridian shows you around the first time you open it, first on your own day and then on an example day.

items.title: Unfinished work rolls over
items.body: Yesterday's open tasks move into today on their own.

items.title: Uninstall removes your data
items.body: Data that used to survive an uninstall is now properly cleared.

items.title: A self-repairing database
items.body: Meridian checks its database at startup and rebuilds a damaged one on its own.

items.title: Quit really quits
items.body: Closing the app now stops the background service with it.

items.title: Pause really pauses
items.body: Pausing no longer puts the background service straight back a few seconds later.

items.title: Honest service status
items.body: Meridian no longer reports its background service as stopped when it is merely busy.

items.title: The damaged-database banner clears
items.body: It now disappears once a repair succeeds, instead of outliving the fix.

items.title: Repair Database works
items.body: Clicking through the repair no longer silently does nothing.

items.title: Three causes of database damage fixed
items.body: The one-time encryption step, running out of file handles, and needless restarts of the background service.

items.title: Work log errors explain themselves
items.body: Approving, rejecting, posting and editing now say why they failed.

items.title: Repair a damaged database in the app
items.body: Your data is salvaged into a fresh file and the damaged copy is kept as a backup.

items.title: The Install button works on Windows
items.body: Claude and Codex now genuinely install rather than just reporting success.

items.title: Startup failures are survivable
items.body: A problem while Meridian is starting no longer takes the whole app down.

items.title: Solo plans are visible again
items.body: Solo users can see their confirmed daily plan.

items.title: First launch just works
items.body: A brand-new install records from its very first launch, with no quit and reopen.

items.title: Clearer encryption warnings
items.body: Meridian no longer claims your data is locked under a lost key when the file is simply empty.

items.title: A behind-the-scenes release
items.body: Build and packaging fixes only, with no change to how Meridian works day to day.

items.title: Move to Applications on first run
items.body: Opened straight from the disk image, Meridian offers to move itself there and reopen.

items.title: Notification permission on Windows
items.body: Setup now asks for it, so reminders work from the start.

items.title: Pauses when your disk is nearly full
items.body: Writing into a full disk is a known way for the database to end up damaged.

items.title: Clearer encryption messages
items.body: If Meridian cannot finish encrypting your data, it says so plainly and tells you how to finish the job.

items.title: Calmer tracker sync
items.body: A passing network glitch no longer looks like a credentials problem.

items.title: Your data is encrypted on disk
items.body: The key lives in your system keychain and your existing data is upgraded automatically.

items.title: Automatic error reports
items.body: Crashes reach us without you reporting them, and you can turn this off in Settings - Capture.

items.title: Nothing identifying leaves your device
items.body: Paths, web addresses, email addresses and your computer's name are stripped before anything is sent.

items.title: AI providers on Windows
items.body: Claude, Codex and Cursor sign in and run the same way they do on a Mac.

items.title: Launch at login repairs itself
items.body: Tracking no longer quietly stops after a restart.

items.title: Simpler notification settings
items.body: One switch plus quiet hours, instead of a list of per-type toggles.

items.title: The background service restarts itself
items.body: Meridian notices within about ten seconds if it stops.

items.title: Tidy up your tasks
items.body: Delete personal tasks, and dismiss or merge the ones Meridian infers from your day.

items.title: Room for 20 tasks a day
items.body: The daily plan now holds twice as many as before.

items.title: A rebuilt daily summary
items.body: Organised around what you planned versus what you actually did, with a progress ring and a single checklist.

items.title: Summaries compose themselves
items.body: Your summary is written at the end of the day, on a screen of its own.

items.title: A work log per ticket
items.body: A tailored update for every ticket you moved forward.

items.title: Secondary monitors are captured
items.body: Meridian reads context from every screen, not only the one you are focused on.

items.title: Act on a tracker from its card
items.body: View tasks and Sync now sit right where the tracker is connected.

items.title: Windows polish
items.body: Your AI provider tools are found, and the popover, tooltips and setup wizard all behave.

items.title: Sign-in across the app
items.body: The dashboard and the tray popover now both require signing in.

items.title: Change a task's status from its detail
items.body: Personal tasks included.

items.title: Choose where a ticket is created
items.body: Pick the tracker a proposed ticket gets filed on.

items.title: Work logs draft themselves
items.body: Once a day, at a time you choose.

items.title: The GitHub project picker saves
items.body: Your board selection now sticks after connecting.

items.title: Windows support
items.body: The background service, tray, notifications and installer all run on Windows.

items.title: Pick a model from a list
items.body: A curated picker, instead of typing the model name yourself.

items.title: Ignore apps and websites
items.body: Choose what Meridian never captures, in Settings.

items.title: Bring your own AI provider
items.body: Add any OpenAI-compatible endpoint from the provider picker.

items.title: An AI-composed daily summary
items.body: It reads like a summary of your day, with the charts chosen to fit what happened.

items.title: A redesigned dashboard
items.body: Refined typography, a single violet accent and real per-app brand colors.

items.title: Sign in with a one-time code
items.body: Just your email, then manage your account from Settings.

items.title: Signed and notarized by Apple
items.body: macOS no longer flags Meridian as an unidentified app.

items.title: Six trackers supported
items.body: GitHub, Linear, Azure DevOps, Jira, Trello and Asana.

items.title: Native GitHub sign-in
items.body: No more copy-pasting a command-line login.

items.title: A live health panel
items.body: Tap the Capturing status in the popover to see it.

items.title: External links open again
items.body: Links from inside the app now reach your browser.

items.title: A one-pager Timeline dashboard
items.body: A brand-new design that puts the whole day on one screen.

items.title: Ticket write-back everywhere
items.body: Broader support across Jira, Linear and Azure DevOps.

roadmap.title: Track down the last cause of database damage on Mac
roadmap.description: Four causes are fixed and Meridian now repairs a damaged database by itself at startup, but we won't call this solved until the machines we're watching stay clean.

roadmap.title: More trackers - Linear, Trello and Azure DevOps
roadmap.description: Meridian already speaks to all three; they stay listed as coming soon until each one is tested end to end.

roadmap.title: Report crashes in the background service
roadmap.description: Error reporting covers the app today, so a hard crash in the background service is only visible in local logs.
